signature_moves: Two-material mood split: dark immersive catalog for choosing sounds vs light quick control panel for using them — one utility, two opposite moods
Presets-as-hardware: audio profiles named/coloured like physical switches ('CherryMX(TM) Japanese Black', 'Everglide(TM) Crystal Purple'), per-switch identity colour on each '+' chip
Audition-before-commit rows: every row pairs a leading '+' (add) with a trailing '▶' (preview) — built around the fact a sound can't be judged from its name
Monochrome control theming + one warm-teal accent: black-filled slider and teal toggle (keycap-black + one candy accent) instead of system blue
defects: Accent not system-bound — master toggle teal + slider black bind to neither controlAccentColor nor each other (brand tell, legitimate house style for a boutique menu-bar utility)

aesthetic.direction: Boutique consumer utility — a warm-cream neo-grotesque brand shell (SF Pro Bold headline, lilac marker highlight, iridescent CD/vinyl wallpaper) wrapped around dark, product-catalog control panels; a remix of Playful/toy warmth with neo-grotesque type discipline, not a stock family
peers: boutique indie menu-bar utilities (polished Control-Center-idiom apps)

psychology: Description-experience gap / demonstrate-don't-describe — the '▶' audition button lets you hear each switch, since a sound is unjudgeable from its name
Jakob's Law — panels mimic Control Center's toggle+slider+list idiom, so the utility is instantly familiar
Von Restorff effect — the single teal toggle is the only saturated element in the light panel; master on/off reads pre-attentively
Hick's Law — sounds chunked under brand sections (CherryMX / Everglide) to reduce scan/decision load
Aesthetic-usability effect — high render polish (iridescent wallpaper, warm glass) buys perceived quality for a tiny utility
Zeigarnik / collectibility — '+' to add sounds to a library gamifies collecting presets like physical switches
